transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Mr Okafor, thank you for coming in with your daughter. How have you been keeping?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Oh, not bad for an old man. My daughter thinks I'm forgetting things. I'm not so sure.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: What sort of things? I'll ask you first, and then Grace.

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Names, mostly. The neighbours' grandchildren. But I've never been good with names.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Grace, what have you noticed?

transcript.speaker: daughter1
transcript.text: It's more than names. He's asked me the same question three or four times in one phone call. That started maybe a year ago, and it's got noticeably worse since Christmas.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Mr Okafor, do you remember that happening?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: No. I don't think I repeat myself. She might be exaggerating a little.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Do you ever forget appointments?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Not that I know of. I write them on the calendar in the kitchen.

transcript.speaker: daughter1
transcript.text: He does write them down, that's true. But he missed his dentist appointment in February because he didn't look at the calendar that day.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Can you tell me what you did yesterday?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Yesterday... Grace came round. We talked about her son's football. I think.

transcript.speaker: daughter1
transcript.text: That was Sunday, Dad. Yesterday was the man about the boiler.

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Ah. Yes, the boiler man. You're right.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: What about older memories, your working life for instance?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Thirty-eight years on the railway. I could tell you every station on the line from here to the coast.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Now, day to day. Who does the cooking?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: I do. I've cooked for myself since my wife passed.

transcript.speaker: daughter1
transcript.text: He does cook, but he's left the gas on twice that I know of. Once in March and once a few weeks ago. I've had a cut-off valve fitted since.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Mr Okafor, were you aware of that?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: She told me about it. I don't remember doing it, to be honest.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: How about money, paying bills, banking?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: I do all that myself.

transcript.speaker: daughter1
transcript.text: He did until last summer. I took over the bills in August after a couple were paid twice. He still does his own shopping with cash.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Are you still driving, Mr Okafor?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Yes, to the shops and to church. Short trips.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Any scrapes, or times you got lost?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: No, never lost.

transcript.speaker: daughter1
transcript.text: There was one time in the spring when he rang me from a petrol station because he wasn't sure which way to go home. It's a route he's driven for years.

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: That was the roadworks. They'd changed everything around.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Grace, were there roadworks?

transcript.speaker: daughter1
transcript.text: There were some, yes. I'm honestly not sure that was all of it.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: How about washing and dressing?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: I manage fine.

transcript.speaker: daughter1
transcript.text: He does. I've got no concerns there.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Mr Okafor, can you tell me today's date?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: It's... Tuesday. The fourteenth? No, sorry, the fifteenth. October.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: And the year?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Twenty twenty-six.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Do you know where we are today?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: The memory clinic at the general hospital. Second floor.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Have you noticed any trouble finding words?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Sometimes a word is on the tip of my tongue. Everybody gets that.

transcript.speaker: daughter1
transcript.text: I've noticed he says the thing a lot more. Like, pass me the thing, when he means the remote.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: How's your mood, Mr Okafor?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: I'm fine. I miss my wife, it's been four years. But I'm not low.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Are you sleeping well?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Like a log. Always have.

transcript.speaker: daughter1
transcript.text: He does nap in the afternoon now, which he never used to.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Grace, has anything changed in his personality?

transcript.speaker: daughter1
transcript.text: Not really. Maybe a bit more irritable when he gets things wrong. But he's still Dad.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Any falls?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: No falls.

transcript.speaker: daughter1
transcript.text: No, none.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: What medicines do you take?

transcript.speaker: patient1
transcript.text: Blood pressure tablets, one in the morning. And a statin.

transcript.speaker: daughter1
transcript.text: He uses a dosette box that I fill on Sundays. He's been good with it.

transcript.speaker: clinician1
transcript.text: Thank you both. Next I'd like to do some formal memory testing.

assessment.label: Memory
assessment.text: Daughter reports repetitive questioning within single phone calls, beginning about a year ago and worsening since Christmas. Mr Okafor acknowledges repeating himself. Recalled the previous day's events accurately. Remote memory for his working life appears preserved.

assessment.label: Daily functioning
assessment.text: Continues to cook; his daughter reports two episodes of leaving the gas on, and a cut-off valve has been fitted. Manages his own finances and pays his bills independently. Became lost on a familiar driving route in the spring. Independent in washing and dressing, which both he and his daughter confirm.

assessment.label: Orientation, language and behaviour
assessment.text: When asked the date, gave it as the fourteenth of October. Correctly named the year and the clinic location. Reports increasingly using vague placeholder words in place of specific nouns. Has begun wandering at night. Findings suggest a mild neurocognitive disorder.
